subject: Re: Early-launch volume bump & phased monthly commit proposal
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia@launchlabs.co>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Jake Wu <jake@launchlabs.co>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Early-launch volume bump & phased monthly commit proposal

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, LaunchLabs is planning a product launch in late September with a large initial ingestion and generation burst during the first 6 weeks, followed by a steadier baseline. I attached our token forecast (LaunchLabs_commit_schedule_v1.xlsx) — the important bits:

- Month 1 (launch month): ~1.2B tokens
- Month 2: ~800M tokens
- Month 3: ~450M tokens
- Months 4–12: average ~150M tokens/month

Key ask: we need a monthly-commit structure that lets us step up (and step down) across months without punitive penalties for the launch burst. Specifically:

- Can Redwood provide a phased/step-up commit (higher for first 2 months, then a staged decline) with per-token discounts that scale by cumulative monthly commit?
- Is there a way to have a small portion of the commit treated as a one-time launch buffer (e.g., flex credit) that doesn’t immediately true-up against penalties if we underconsume later?
- We may need a short evaluation window for internal experimentation — can evaluation traffic (non-production) be exempt or discounted for the first 1M tokens/month?

Also curious about payment terms (Net-60 vs Net-30) and if there are seasonality accommodations for Q4 spikes. We’re sensitive to committing too high for months 4–12 but don’t want to be throttled during the initial go-live.

Appreciate a proposal with simple, explainable economics (example monthly numbers + discounts + any credits). Attached forecast for your reference. Happy to hop on another 30-min sync.

Best,
Olivia Chen
Head of ML
LaunchLabs

Attachment: LaunchLabs_commit_schedule_v1.xlsx
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@launchlabs.co>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Early-launch volume bump & phased monthly commit proposal

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear forecast and the call. I reviewed the attached schedule and sketched a phased commit option that balances launch flexibility with predictable unit economics. High-level proposal (summary):

- Structure: 3-step monthly commit with an initial "Launch Buffer" that is credited against Month 1 and Month 2 usage. Launch Buffer = 25% of Month 1 commit (non-refundable credit applied to first two months).
- Monthly commit schedule (example based on your forecast):
  - Month 1: 1.0B committed tokens (Launch Buffer adds equivalent of 250M tokens credit)
  - Month 2: 700M committed tokens
  - Month 3: 400M committed tokens
  - Months 4–12: 150M committed tokens/month (can be adjusted after Q4)
- Discounting (per-token):
  - Base price for hosted API: $0.000020 / token
  - Cumulative volume discount tiers (applied on monthly committed consumption):
    - >1B tokens/month: 12% discount
    - >3B tokens/month: 18% discount
    - >5B tokens/month: 22% discount (negotiable for committed 12-month upfront)
- Roll-forward: unused committed tokens within a quarter may be rolled forward to the next month within that quarter only (not year-long). Annual true-up applies at year-end.
- Evaluation traffic: we can mark up to 1M tokens/month as trial/exempt for the first 3 months (no charge).
- Payment terms: standard Net-30, but we can consider Net-60 for first invoice for enterprise procurement (subject to credit review).

Next steps:
1) Marissa — can you draft a short SOW (1–2 pages) with the mechanics above and add a Launch Buffer clause? Please attach to the HubSpot deal.
2) Rishi — can you confirm whether the >5B top-tier discount is approvable as-is or needs leadership sign-off?
3) Olivia — if the above looks directionally good, let’s schedule a 30-min touchpoint to finalize numbers and payment timing. I attached a draft SOW for review (Redwood_SOW_Draft_v2.pdf).

If you’d like a different split on the Launch Buffer (e.g., larger one-time credit vs longer roll-forward window), let me know and we can iterate.

Talk soon,
Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_SOW_Draft_v2.pdf, link to HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/LL-2026-048

On Thu, Jul 15, 2026 at 10:05 AM Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear forecast and the call. I reviewed the attached schedule and sketched a phased commit option that balances launch flexibility with predictable unit economics. High-level proposal (summary):
> ...

Monica / Team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the useful proposal. A few clarifying points from LaunchLabs:

- The Launch Buffer concept looks promising. Can the buffer be consumed across Month 1 and Month 2 without shifting discounts thresholds (i.e., buffer consumption counts toward cumulative monthly tiers)?
- For the evaluation traffic exemption, we only need it for the first 6 weeks of internal testing; can you make that a one-time 1.5M token exemption rather than 1M/month for 3 months?
- Regarding roll-forward: instead of quarter-only roll-forward, would Redwood consider a 6-week window post-launch to allow us to smooth spikes into Month 2?
- If we agree to the 12-month commit schedule, would Redwood consider Net-60 on billing and an upfront $25k launch credit applied to the first invoice?
- Finally — can you confirm the penalty mechanics for underutilization? We prefer a true-up model (pay for shortfall at month-end at the negotiated per-token price) rather than automatic forfeiture.

We can do a 30-min call next week. Appreciate any flexibility on the buffer and payment terms.

Best,
Jake Wu
Director of Platform
LaunchLabs
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 16:35:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Early-launch volume bump & phased monthly commit proposal

Folks — forwarding the customer thread. Key asks to bake into our counterproposal:

- Make the Launch Buffer explicitly consumable across Month 1 and Month 2 and count toward discount thresholds (customer wants buffer to help hit higher-tier discounts during launch).
- Swap the eval exemption to a one-time 1.5M token credit for the pre-launch testing window.
- Offer a 6-week roll-forward window (instead of quarter) for unused committed tokens tied specifically to the launch period.
- Approve Net-60 for the first invoice; finance may require a credit review but I expect we can accommodate for a named enterprise. Also propose a $25k launch credit applied to invoice #1 (discount against committed spend).
- Penalty mechanics: customer prefers month-end true-up at negotiated price; avoid forfeiture language. Draft the SOW redlines to reflect this.

Proposed counterpricing (internal):
- Base price: $0.000020 / token
- Discount tiers (monthly committed consumption): >1B = 10% discount, >3B = 16% discount, >5B = 20% discount.
- Launch Buffer = 25% of Month 1 commit as a credit (applied to M1+M2 consumption).
- $25k one-time launch credit on invoice #1.

Marissa — please prepare SOW redlines (attach Redwood_SOW_Draft_v2_redline.pdf) and put the updated docs into HubSpot. Rishi — please confirm pricing approval for the 20% top-tier discount or escalate to pricing committee if needed. I’ll take point on commercial call with LaunchLabs once docs are updated.

Thanks,
Monica
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
